questions.question: Inside the body of a `for` loop, what does `next` do when R executes it?
options: It ends the whole loop, and R continues with the code after the loop.
It skips the rest of the current pass and starts the next pass.
It skips the following pass, so the loop jumps over one element.
It restarts the loop from the first element of its vector.

questions.question: Which statement about a `repeat { ... }` loop in R is correct?
options: It checks a condition before each pass, like a `while` loop.
It runs its body a fixed number of times, given in its header.
It stops by itself once a pass leaves every variable unchanged.
It runs its body again and again until a `break` in it is executed.

questions.question: A `for (i in 1:5)` loop has a `break` in its body that is not inside any `if`. What happens when the loop runs?
options: The loop ends during its first pass; the lines after `break` never run.
R ignores the `break`, since it has no condition attached to it.
Every pass runs up to `break`, and the lines after it are skipped.
R stops with an error, since `break` must be used inside an `if`.

questions.question: Which line, inserted before `print(i)` in the body of `for (i in 1:6) { print(i) }`, makes the loop print 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6?
options: `if (i == 3) break`
`if (i != 3) next`
`if (i == 3) next`
`if (i == 4) next`

questions.question: With `v <- c(4, 7, -1, 5)`, what is `s` after `s <- 0; for (x in v) { if (x < 0) break; s <- s + x }`?
What is `n` after `n <- 0; repeat { n <- n + 1; if (n >= 4) break }`?
options: no value, since `repeat` loops for ever

questions.question: What is `k` after `k <- 10; repeat { k <- k + 1; if (k > 5) break }`?
Which values does `for (i in 1:5) { if (i == 2) next; if (i == 4) break; print(i) }` print?
options: 1 only
1, 3 and 5
1 and 3
1, 2 and 3

questions.question: What is `total` after `i <- 0; total <- 0; while (i < 5) { i <- i + 1; if (i == 3) next; total <- total + i }`?
options: no value, since `next` makes the loop hang

questions.question: What is `i` after `for (i in 1:10) { if (i^2 > 20) break }`?

The square-root method updates a guess `g` to `g_new <- 0.5 * (g + a / g)` and stops once `abs(g_new - g)` is at most a tolerance. Why does a `repeat` loop with its `break` test at the end of the body suit this method?
options: `repeat` stops by itself once the guesses no longer change.
`repeat` cannot run forever, unlike a `while` loop.
The change exists only after a new guess, and the test comes after it.
`repeat` runs faster than `while`, since it checks no condition.

questions.question: A loop meant to stop when `i` reaches 5 is written `i <- 0; while (i < 5) { if (i == 2) next; i <- i + 1 }`. What happens when it runs?
options: It ends with `i` equal to 5, after skipping the pass for 2.
It never ends: from `i` equal to 2 on, `next` skips the update.
It ends with `i` equal to 2, because `next` leaves the `while` loop.
It ends with `i` equal to 4, because the update for 2 is skipped once.

questions.question: What is `c(x, iter)` after `x <- 1; iter <- 0; repeat { x <- x + 2; iter <- iter + 1; if (x == 10 | iter >= 6) break }`?
options: no value, since `x` is never equal to 10

questions.question: What is `count` after `count <- 0; for (i in 1:3) { for (j in 1:3) { if (j == 2) break; count <- count + 1 } }`?
What is `i` after `i <- 1; while (i < 100) { i <- i * 3; if (i == 50) break }`?
options: no value, since the `break` is unreachable

questions.question: In the nested loops `total <- 0; for (i in 1:3) { if (i == 2) next; for (j in 1:2) total <- total + 1 }`, what is `total` at the end?
A student writes `x <- 0; repeat { x <- x + 2; if (x == 7) break }`. Which statement about this loop is correct?
options: It stops with `x` equal to 8, the first value past 7.
It stops with `x` equal to 6, the last value before 7.
It stops after one pass, since `repeat` runs its body at least once.
It never stops: `x` is always even, so `x == 7` is never `TRUE`.

questions.question: Which `repeat` loop always ends with the same `x` as `while (x < 50) x <- x * 2`, for every positive starting value of `x`?
options: `repeat { if (x >= 50) break; x <- x * 2 }`
`repeat { x <- x * 2; if (x >= 50) break }`
`repeat { x <- x * 2; if (x < 50) break }`
`repeat { if (x < 50) break; x <- x * 2 }`

questions.question: For a numeric vector `x` without missing values and `s <- 0`, which loop always leaves the same `s` as `for (v in x) { if (v < 0) next; s <- s + v }`?
options: `for (v in x) { if (v < 0) break; s <- s + v }`
`for (v in x) { s <- s + v; if (v < 0) next }`
`for (v in x) { if (v >= 0) s <- s + v }`
`for (v in x) { if (v < 0) s <- s + v }`

questions.question: What is `i` after `i <- 0; repeat { i <- i + 1; if (i == 5) next; if (i >= 5) break }`?
options: no value, since `next` traps the loop
